coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 55 days out and in taper—this is your Saturday long run, but scaled. Target 90–100 minutes at Z2 (130–145 bpm based on your recent 125 bpm baseline), with 800–1200m of vert incorporated naturally via rolling terrain or a single sustained climb. Skip the ego; the fitness is there. Your last long effort was 17.16 miles on 2026-07-13 (12 days ago), so you're due for a moderate-length alpine-specific stimulus—not a peak day, but not a jog either. Recovery score of 83 means you're ready to run, but not to exceed.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat a real breakfast 2–3 hours pre-run (oats, fruit, protein). For a 90–100 minute Z2 run with climbing, carry 30–45g of simple carbs (gels, chews, or sports drink) and drink to thirst—you're in alpine terrain where aid is sparse, so this is a dress rehearsal for race pacing and stomach tolerance. Post-run, get carbs + protein (3:1 ratio) within 60 minutes; your sleep efficiency is already at 95.3%, so nutrient timing matters more than volume right now.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is solid at 7.88h and resting HR is 60 bpm (down from your 30-day avg of 62.2)—you're adapting well. Tonight, prioritize 8+ hours and skip late caffeine. Ice bath optional; at this point in taper, sleep and glycogen repletion outweigh cold water immersion. Sunday should be fully easy (45–60 min Z1–Z2) or rest entirely—taper means you're protecting the nervous system now, not pushing it.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 8 weeks from Slovenia and entering the sprint phase where execution matters more than volume. Use today's run to practice your race-day fueling strategy and test your mental pacing—the Julian Alps 50K will demand sustained effort on thin air and sparse aid, so every practice run is a simulation. Stay composed; you've built the base, and taper is when doubt creeps in. Trust the training and focus on sharp, intentional efforts over the next 7 weeks.
